name: 肉の店 牛見 (Niku no Mise Ushimi)

claims.text: The beef cutlet is breaded in wheat panko and fried; no dedicated fryer for gluten-free items is indicated. All fried items (croquettes, cutlets) are prepared in the same kitchen.
Sauces including ginger sauce and balsamic house sauce are house-made; no information confirms they are wheat-free. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
This is a meat butcher shop and the deli/lunch counter handles beef, pork, and chicken throughout. No plant-based items are produced in a separate area.

name: 小川の庄 大門店 (Ogawa no Sho Daimon-ten)

claims.text: The entire menu is based on wheat-flour dough. Wheat is listed as a primary declared allergen. There is no separate preparation area or alternative dough for gluten-free orders. Cross-contamination risk is inherent and unavoidable.

The nozawana filling is seasoned with house-made miso and soy sauce (醤油). Standard Japanese soy sauce and many miso varieties contain wheat as a fermentation ingredient. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

Pork and dairy are listed as declared allergens on the company's allergen sheet, suggesting some product variants contain these ingredients. Shared irori grilling surface and preparation areas mean contact with non-vegan items cannot be excluded.

No documented allergy protocol or staff allergy-handling procedure found in public sources. The experience-oriented format (guests cook alongside staff) may allow for some dialogue, but formal allergen accommodation is not offered.
Standard fillings — nozawana greens, azuki red bean, pumpkin, mushroom-vegetable mix — are vegetable-based with no meat. No fish or meat ingredients are documented in the core lineup.
The company explicitly avoids preservatives and artificial colourings, sourcing from low-pesticide, small-scale local farms.

name: 太田屋 助右衛門 (Otaya Sukeemon)

claims.text: Both 80% wheat-containing zaru soba and 100% buckwheat juzen soba are prepared in the same kitchen; no separation protocol has been documented.
Tempura (wheat batter) is a menu item; fryer separation from buckwheat items is not confirmed.
The tsuyu dipping sauce is described as soy-based; no mention of tamari or wheat-free soy sauce anywhere in available sources. Standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat.
Tsuyu almost certainly contains katsuobushi (bonito) dashi — no kombu-only or vegan dashi option is documented.
Tempura set includes shrimp; egg roll slices accompany lunch sets — fish and egg present in the kitchen.
The 十善そば noodles themselves are made from 100% buckwheat flour with no wheat added — the purest buckwheat noodle on the menu.
Stone-mill self-grinding means full traceability of the buckwheat flour used in the noodles.
グルテンフリー対応や交差汚染防止策の記載なし。精進料理ベースではあるが、厨房での小麦使用状況は不明。
醤油（小麦含有）の使用が料理に含まれる可能性があるが、使用する醤油の種類（小麦あり・なし）について公式の言及なし。
隠れ動物性食材（かつおだし・みりん等）の有無について非公開。精進料理の伝統的手法に従っていればヴィーガン対応の可能性が高いが、要確認。
アレルギー対応方針の明示なし。問い合わせ先：026-234-0001（大勧進）またはcontact@tsumugi-wb.co.jp
精進料理をベースとしたメニューは動物性食材を最小限に抑える伝統に沿っており、植物性食材中心の食事が期待できる。
寺粥御膳は根菜の煮物や豆腐など植物性食材を中心とした構成と複数のレビューが報告している。
Nihachi soba contains 20% wheat flour; noodles are not gluten-free. No dedicated GF station or protocol has been reported at this restaurant.

Dipping broth (tsuyu) is made with katsuo-bushi and almost certainly standard wheat-containing soy sauce, as is universal at traditional Japanese soba shops. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
All soba broth is bonito-based. No kombu-only or vegan dashi option is indicated. Tamago-yaki (egg) is a signature side. Cross-contact with animal products throughout the kitchen.

Staff do not speak foreign languages; no allergy-handling protocol has been documented for this restaurant. Diners with serious allergies should call ahead (026-232-5347) with a Japanese-speaking contact.
The restaurant holds an English menu, making basic communication slightly easier for foreign visitors, though dietary restriction conversations would require Japanese.

name: おやきと漬物の専門店 あづみ堂 (Oyaki to Tsukemono no Senmonten Azumido)

claims.text: 製造工場ではそば・乳成分・卵・くるみを含む製品を製造しており、交差汚染のリスクがある（全品のアレルゲン表示に共通記載）。
そば皮おやき野沢菜の原材料に「醤油」「味噌」が含まれ、アレルゲンとして小麦・大豆を表示。米粉もっちりおやきも「小麦グルテン」を使用しており、全品小麦を含む。
豚・牛・鶏を使った餡と同じ製造設備を共用。野菜系の餡でも工場内での交差汚染が否定できない。
アレルゲン情報は公式サイトの品目別ページで公開されているが、店頭でのアレルギー対応については情報なし。予約不可・対応スタッフへの事前相談は困難な業態。
公式サイトに全品目のアレルゲン一覧ページが整備されており、原材料を事前に確認できる。

name: パティスリー HEIGORO 本店 (Pâtisserie HEIGORO Honten)

claims.text: All café kakigori flavors list 小麦 (wheat) as a confirmed allergen. Pastry production shares the same kitchen environment used for wheat-based cakes, tarts, scones, and baked goods — cross-contamination risk is high for any gluten-sensitive diner.

No soy sauce used in this dessert/patisserie context, but wheat is present throughout via flour-based pastries, sablés, scones, tart shells, and kakigori syrups. Wheat is a confirmed allergen in all tested menu items.

Dairy is foundational to the menu — butter, cream, fromage blanc, condensed milk, Jersey milk soft-serve, and mascarpone appear across all product categories. Egg is also listed as a confirmed allergen in all kakigori items. There is no plant-based section or vegan-friendly preparation track.

One source notes that advance reservations (at least 2 days prior) may allow for some allergy accommodation — contact directly at 026-266-0156 or heigoro@fujiyagohonjin.co.jp to discuss specific needs before visiting.
Allergen information is displayed on café menu items (dairy, eggs, wheat, almonds, soy listed per item), allowing diners to identify specific allergens before ordering.

name: パスタと自然派ワイン こまつや (Pasta to Natural Wine Komatsuya)

claims.text: The kitchen makes all pasta in-house using Shinshu wheat flour. There is no documented gluten-free preparation area and cross-contamination with wheat is essentially unavoidable.
No allergen menu is published. Soy sauce (which typically contains wheat) may appear in some preparations; the restaurant has not disclosed ingredient-level details publicly.
Animal-based ingredients (meat, fish, cheese, eggs, butter) are present throughout the kitchen. No separation for vegan preparation is indicated.

TripAdvisor reviewers confirm staff can modify dishes on request — for example removing sausage from the porcini tagliatelle — when informed in advance. Reservations via LINE or phone allow advance communication of restrictions.
The menu is genuinely vegetable-forward: Shinshu organic produce features prominently in most dishes, and the kitchen uses locally sourced organic ingredients throughout.
Reservations via official LINE (lin.ee/b64Mej3) allow guests to communicate dietary needs before arrival, and the intimate 13-seat counter setting means staff are very attentive.
